chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Yaqoub ibn Yazeed, from Al-Husayn ibn Bashaar Al-Wasity, who said:

I wrote to Abu Al-Hasan Al-Reza (peace be upon him), 'There is a relative of mine who has proposed to me, and there is something (bad) in his character/manners.' So he (peace be upon him) said: 'Do not give him in marriage if he is of bad character.'
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on marrying a relative with bad character?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from Imam Al-Reza (peace be upon him), the criterion of 'khuluq' (moral character) is elevated above familial ties, advising against marrying a relative if their conduct is deficient. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on moral integrity as a prerequisite for marital harmony, prioritizing spiritual compatibility over mere lineage or proximity. The Imam’s direct instruction underscores that good character is not merely a social virtue but a religious necessity for a successful union.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Biin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Yaqoub Bin Yazeed, from Al Husayn Bin Bashaar Al Wasity who said,

‘I wrote to Abu Al-Hassan Al-Reza<sup>asws</sup>, ‘There is a relative of mine who has sent a proposal to me, and in his mannerisms there is something (bad)’. So he<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Do not give in marriage to him if there was evilness in the mannerisms’.
en.sarwar: 30. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ya’qub ibn Yazid from al-Husayn ibn Bashshar al-Wasitiy who has said the following: “

I once wrote to abu al-Hassan al-Rida’, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked, ‘One of my relatives has proposed for marriage but there is something in his moral manners. He (the Imam) said, ‘You must not give in marriage if his moral manners are bad/”
